mainEntity.name: What is the difference between single-pane, double-pane, and triple-pane windows?

acceptedAnswer.text: The primary difference lies in the number of glass layers and their insulating properties. Single-pane windows, the oldest type, have just one layer of glass and offer minimal insulation, leading to significant heat loss or gain. Double-pane windows feature two layers of glass separated by a sealed air or gas-filled space, greatly improving insulation and energy efficiency. Triple-pane windows add a third layer of glass and another air/gas space, providing the highest level of insulation, sound reduction, and energy savings, though at a higher cost.
acceptedAnswer.description: Single-pane windows have one glass layer, offering minimal insulation. Double-pane have two glass layers with an air/gas space for better insulation. Triple-pane adds a third layer, providing the best insulation and sound reduction.
